title: This Fake Transaction Can Trick You Into Sending Crypto to a Scammer
caption: Educational only. Not financial advice. Address poisoning: scammers send a tiny transfer from a look-alike wallet address so it shows up in your history, hoping you copy it by mistake. Sources: MetaMask support, Ledger Academy, Trezor support. AI-generated voice. Did you know about this trick? Educational only. Not financial advice.

scenes.head: SCAM WARNING
scenes.hook: A FAKE TRANSACTION CAN EMPTY YOUR WALLET
scenes.narration: A fake transaction can trick you into sending crypto to a scammer.

scenes.head: THE TRICK
scenes.hook: SCAMMERS COPY THE START AND END OF AN ADDRESS
scenes.narration: Scammers create a wallet address that looks almost the same as one you used, matching the first and last characters. Then they send you a tiny transfer.

scenes.head: THE TRAP
scenes.hook: THEIR ADDRESS NOW SITS IN YOUR HISTORY
scenes.narration: The look-alike address now appears in your history. If you copy it from there by mistake, your money goes to them.

scenes.head: THE FIX
scenes.hook: CHECK EVERY CHARACTER BEFORE YOU SEND
scenes.narration: Never copy an address from your history. Use a saved address book, and compare the full address before you confirm.
